name: The Hairspring Vigil

detectability.signature: Flatlined entropy gradient at the boundary wrapped in a faint silver temporal shear halo

proximity: Engine noise stretches into long, muffled tones
Onboard clocks lag behind fleet standard by a few seconds
contact: Motion becomes dreamlike and effortful inside the stillness
Hull micro-vibrations freeze mid-cycle, audible as one sustained note
prolonged_exposure: Biological aging nearly suspended for everything within
Desynchronization from normal spacetime upon exit, lasting days

phenomena: Dust and debris hanging in perfect suspension
Visible echoes of past events frozen mid-motion at the boundary
Aging and de-aging of biological matter arrested entirely
opportunities: Emergency refuge for damaged vessels fleeing pursuit
Chance to study rare phenomena of near-perfect stasis
known_incidents: The hospital ship Mercy of Gears hid inside for three weeks while pursuers circled outside, its patients aging not a day
description: The Vigil appears as a silvered sphere of held breath nearly two thousand kilometers across, its surface a faint halo where starlight seems to hesitate before committing. Dust, debris, and the occasional ancient probe hang motionless within like insects in amber. Sensors read its edge as a flatline: entropy simply stops being interesting there.

Crossing the boundary feels like sinking through cold glass. Motion inside remains possible but slow, sound decays into single sustained tones, and every action carries the weight of a decision made once and kept. Nothing inside ages; nothing inside hurries; nothing inside changes unless visitors bring the change with them.

Ninety million years ago a collapsing gas shell stalled mid-detonation for reasons models still cannot reproduce, leaving this permanent pause. The hospital ship Mercy of Gears made the site famous by sheltering inside for three weeks while raiders circled the perimeter, then emerging to patients untouched and pursuers gone stale.

Refugees, smugglers with perishable cargo, and one very patient hospice order all keep coordinates to the Vigil close. Researchers drift at the boundary taking the same measurements repeatedly, since repetition is the only experiment it permits. It has watched the stars for ninety million years without blinking, and it shows no sign of starting.
